elements.element: Renewal must occur either only by mutual written agreement or, if automatic, in successive 12-month periods.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 provides for automatic renewal for an additional one-year period on each anniversary.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may prevent renewal by giving no more than 30 days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: Automatic renewal applies, but the Company must give 60 days' prior written notice rather than 30 days.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must provide a renewal reminder 60 days before each renewal.
elements.evidence: No operative language requires HDI to provide any renewal reminder.

elements.element: Price increases must be capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: Neither Section 4.1 nor Section 3.1 contains this price-increase cap.
Section 4.1 expressly provides for automatic one-year renewals.

elements.element: The non-renewal notice window for automatic renewal must be no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: The Company has a 60-day notice period, but HDI remains subject to a 90-day period. Thus the operative clause includes a non-renewal notice window exceeding 60 days.

elements.element: Price increases must be capped at 5% or less.
elements.evidence: No operative provision caps price increases at 5% or less.

result.reason: The redline shortens only the Company's notice period. It omits the preferred 30-day opt-out, Vendor reminder, and CPI/3% cap, and it retains HDI's 90-day notice period and no 5% cap. It therefore reaches neither complete position. The targeted change does not disturb the unrelated compensation provision, although Section 4.1 remains framed as a general termination right rather than clearly as notice of non-renewal.
